objects.original: A completed scalar Ito integral, progressive weight and literal product integrand.
objects.reconstructed: Write R_+=[0,infinity), and let lambda_T be Lebesgue measure on [0,T], transported to R_+ (the given comap of volume restricted to [0,T]). All time integrals below use this measure unless indicated otherwise. For n in N put t[n,i]=i*T/2^n for i=0,...,2^n, and Delta_i^n Z=Z(t[n,i+1])-Z(t[n,i]). A ProgressiveL2Integrand eta on horizon T is a real process eta(t,omega), strongly progressive for the filtration, with (omega,t) -> eta(t,omega) in L^2(mu x lambda_T). Let I_T(eta) be the completed continuous Ito integral driven by the explicitly given scalar B: limit of elementary approximations off the null uniform-Cauchy bad set, patched to zero there, constant after T.
objects.evidence: AutoSamplingTheory/TechnicalLemmas/StochasticProcesses/ItoWeightedRiemannSums.lean:232; The original eta and driver B are retained in every cell multiplier and terminal integral.

domains.original: Finite sample measure, usual filtration, T>0 and same scalar Brownian driver.
domains.reconstructed: Omega measurable with ambient sigma-algebra m; mu finite; filtration on R_+; T>0; B:R_+ x Omega->R; eta progressive L^2 on T; w:R_+ x Omega->R; C real.
domains.evidence: AutoSamplingTheory/TechnicalLemmas/StochasticProcesses/ItoWeightedRiemannSums.lean:232; Section parameters introduce no extra data beyond the source setup.

quantifiers.original: Given eta,w,C, there exists theta; its process equality is for all times/samples, followed by convergence.
quantifiers.reconstructed: Universally Omega,m,filtration,mu,T,B,eta,hT,hB,hUsual,w,hw,hCont,C,hBound; then there exists theta in ProgressiveL2Integrand(filtration,mu,T); then pointwise identity for all t,omega and convergence as n->infinity.
quantifiers.evidence: AutoSamplingTheory/TechnicalLemmas/StochasticProcesses/ItoWeightedRiemannSums.lean:232; The existential theta is returned before both the global identity and in-measure conclusion.

assumptions.original: eta product-L²; w globally progressive, a.e. continuous on [0,T], and |w|≤C pointwise on the horizon.
assumptions.reconstructed: For each finite family of times, the corresponding B-values have the centered joint Gaussian law with covariance Cov(B_s,B_t)=min(s,t). The paths of B are mu-a.e. continuous; in particular B_0=0 almost surely, with no pointwise initial-value requirement. B is strongly adapted, and every increment B_t-B_s, s<=t, is independent of filtration(s). The filtration is right continuous, and every mu-null subset of Omega belongs to filtration(t) for every t>=0 (completeness at each time). The process w is strongly progressive, its paths are continuous on [0,T] for mu-a.e. omega, and |w(t,omega)|<=C for every t<=T and every omega.
assumptions.evidence: AutoSamplingTheory/TechnicalLemmas/StochasticProcesses/ItoWeightedRiemannSums.lean:232; hLift/hW derive product-space essential boundedness from the public horizon bound and progressivity.

conclusion.original: Left-weighted dyadic integral increments converge in measure to the completed terminal integral of theta=w eta.
conclusion.reconstructed: There exists theta with theta(t,omega)=w(t,omega)*eta(t,omega) for every t>=0 and every omega, and the sums sum_i w(t[n,i],omega)*(I_T(eta)(t[n,i+1],omega)-I_T(eta)(t[n,i],omega)) converge in mu-measure to I_T(theta)(T,omega).
conclusion.evidence: AutoSamplingTheory/TechnicalLemmas/StochasticProcesses/ItoWeightedRiemannSums.lean:232; Private assemble_integrands gives literal finite sums; hAppIto identifies exact weighted increments and terminal isometry supplies convergence.

scopes.original: Literal theta globally; hypotheses controlling size and paths only on [0,T].
scopes.reconstructed: The identity defining theta holds for all nonnegative times, including beyond T. The bound and path continuity hypotheses apply only on [0,T]. Convergence is in measure at the single terminal horizon T; no L^p or pathwise convergence assertion is made.
scopes.evidence: AutoSamplingTheory/TechnicalLemmas/StochasticProcesses/ItoWeightedRiemannSums.lean:232; hTime restricts domination to (0,T]; t=0 is ignored only in product-measure approximation, not in theta's pointwise identity.

constant_dependencies.original: C uniform in t and omega; no rate.
constant_dependencies.reconstructed: C is a given common real bound independent of time and sample point on [0,T]; no separate C>=0 assumption is written. theta can depend on all preceding data. There is no rate constant.
constant_dependencies.evidence: AutoSamplingTheory/TechnicalLemmas/StochasticProcesses/ItoWeightedRiemannSums.lean:232; K=|C| and (2K)² are internal domination constants.
